items.q: What is the luminosity of a star with a radius of 0.5 solar radii and a temperature of 3,800 K?
items.reply: The star's luminosity is 0.04696 solar luminosities (L = R² (T / 5772 K)⁴ in solar units: R = 0.5 solar radii, T = 3800 K; Stefan-Boltzmann law). [stars]

items.q: A planet transits a star of 0.4 solar radii with a depth of 2,500 ppm. What is the planet's radius in Earth radii?
items.reply: The planet's radius is 2.182 Earth radii (R_p = R_star √depth: R_star = 0.4 solar radii = 43.63 Earth radii, depth 2500 ppm; limb darkening ignored). [transits]

items.q: What is the orbital period, in days, of a planet 0.05 AU from a star of 0.3 solar masses?
items.reply: The orbital period is 7.456 days (Kepler's third law, P = √(a³ / M) years: a = 0.05 AU, M = 0.3 solar masses; 1 year = 365.25 days, circular orbit, planet mass neglected). [exoorbits]

items.q: How much starlight does a planet 0.2 AU from a star of 0.04 solar luminosities receive, compared with Earth?
items.reply: The planet receives 1 times the starlight Earth gets from the Sun (S = L / a²: L = 0.04 solar luminosities, a = 0.2 AU; inverse-square law). [exoorbits]

items.q: What is the transit probability, in percent, of a planet 0.1 AU from a star of 0.6 solar radii?

items.q: What is the equilibrium temperature of a planet 0.1 AU from a star of 0.01 solar luminosities, with an albedo of 0.3?
